paragraphs.sourceText: In her second year, Charlene Duong learned of the use of poisonous, synthetic pesticides on her college campus. Shocked but not surprised, she knew she had to do something. Along with a couple of classmates, Charlene did a quick web search and discovered a small but growing movement led by the organization, Herbicide-Free Campus (HFC), to rid college campuses of artificial herbicide (灭草剂). They were 26 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 在大二的时候，夏琳·杜 (Charlene Duong) 了解到她的大学校园里使用了有毒的合成农药。她感到震惊，但并不惊讶，她知道自己必须做点什么。夏琳和几个同学一起快速进行了网络搜索，发现了由“无除草剂校园”（HFC）组织领导的一项规模虽小但不断发展的运动，旨在消除大学校园中的人工除草剂（灭草剂）。他们很感兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: Like many, Charlene experiences climate anxiety — a 27 fear of a climate catastrophe — and was, at the time, looking for an 28 . When she discovered the HFC movement, she said she felt she “had found a specific area to focus on that still fit into the larger picture of fighting for a healthier, safer, cleaner 29 for all.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 和许多人一样，夏琳也经历过气候焦虑——对气候灾难的长期恐惧——并且当时正在寻找发泄的途径。当她发现 HFC 运动时，她说她觉得自己“找到了一个值得关注的特定领域，该领域仍然适合为所有人争取更健康、更安全、更清洁的环境的大局。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Toxic herbicide use in university land care is not unique. Most institutions of higher education rely on synthetic pesticides and fertilizers to achieve 30 goals. Having a “beautiful” campus means green and perfectly maintained lawns along with flower beds and paved sidewalks. But these 31 managed campuses can come at a cost: increased cancer risk, 32 waterways, poisoned wildlife and lifeless soil.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大学土地护理中使用有毒除草剂的现象并非独一无二。大多数高等教育机构依靠合成农药和化肥来实现审美目标。拥有“美丽”的校园意味着绿色且维护良好的草坪、花坛和铺好的人行道。但这些传统管理的校园可能会付出代价：癌症风险增加、水道被污染、野生动物中毒和土壤毫无生气。

paragraphs.sourceText: Pesticide use on college campuses also contributes to our global climate crisis. The use of chemicals to get rid of insects or unwanted plant life can increase indirect 33 , as they can include petroleum-based ingredients. Pesticide use also decreases the life in soil, 34 the ability of soils to absorb carbon or retain water and thus reducing campuses’ ability to recover quickly from climate-related extreme weather events like droughts and floods.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大学校园使用杀虫剂也加剧了我们的全球气候危机。使用化学品来消灭昆虫或不需要的植物会增加间接排放，因为它们可能包含石油基成分。农药的使用还会减少土壤的寿命，阻碍土壤吸收碳或保留水分的能力，从而降低校园从干旱和洪水等与气候相关的极端天气事件中快速恢复的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Instead of using toxic chemicals, students working with HFC help out with 35 the campus grounds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 使用 HFC 的学生不使用有毒化学品，而是帮助清理校园的杂草。

paragraphs.sourceText: “This work reminds me to be in the present moment as I play my role in reducing herbicide use and keeping my campus safe and healthy,” says Charlene.
paragraphs.translationZh: “这项工作提醒我要活在当下，在减少除草剂使用和保持校园安全健康方面发挥自己的作用，”夏琳说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why Your Library Is the Most Important Place in Town
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么您的图书馆是城里最重要的地方

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Librarians know the value of their community services, and their patrons appreciate their importance as well. But in an increasingly digital world, we see the role of libraries as community and cultural centers at times undervalued. When shrinking municipal budgets combine with the nonstop technological revolution, public library services that focus on building communities face-to-face, inspiring and educating patrons about art, literature, and music, and helping patrons engage in civil discourse can seem old-fashioned. But it is precisely those shrinking budgets and the assault of technologically mediated life that make public libraries’ cultural and community offerings more important than ever.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 图书馆员知道他们的社区服务的价值，他们的顾客也认识到它们的重要性。但在日益数字化的世界中，我们发现图书馆作为社区和文化中心的作用有时被低估。当不断缩减的市政预算与不间断的技术革命相结合时，专注于面对面建设社区、启发和教育顾客有关艺术、文学和音乐以及帮助顾客参与公民对话的公共图书馆服务似乎已经过时了。但正是预算的缩减和以技术为媒介的生活的冲击，使得公共图书馆的文化和社区服务比以往任何时候都更加重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Many people point out the value public libraries bring to their communities. More than just books and banks of computers, libraries are still places where individuals gather to explore, interact, and imagine. Some of the specific ways in which libraries add value to our communities and serve as cultural centers for our patrons are community builders, centers for the arts, and champions of youth. Libraries serve in these capacities and are more than just about information.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 许多人指出公共图书馆为其社区带来的价值。图书馆不仅仅是书籍和电脑库，它仍然是人们聚集探索、互动和想象的地方。图书馆为我们的社区增加价值并作为我们顾客的文化中心的一些具体方式是社区建设者、艺术中心和青年捍卫者。图书馆发挥这些作用，并且不仅仅提供信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) As community builders libraries are engaged in incredible work. From tiny public libraries to huge city institutions with multiple branches, libraries across the United States are building community and supporting local culture in exciting ways. These are inspiring and hopefully will encourage librarians interested in community services and cultural outreach to make connections with each other, share ideas, and build partnerships. Supporters of libraries as community builders claim that unless you are out there changing neighborhoods, you are not completing the work you are to do. Strengthening neighborhoods and championing the cultural lives of communities are big responsibilities.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 作为社区建设者，图书馆正在从事令人难以置信的工作。从小型公共图书馆到拥有多个分支机构的大型城市机构，美国各地的图书馆正在以令人兴奋的方式建设社区并支持当地文化。这些都是鼓舞人心的，希望能够鼓励对社区服务和文化推广感兴趣的图书馆员相互联系、分享想法并建立伙伴关系。支持图书馆作为社区建设者的人声称，除非你出去改变社区，否则你就没有完成你要做的工作。加强社区建设和倡导社区文化生活是一项重大责任。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Place-based economic development stresses the importance of offering attractive, functional, and community-based places, such as libraries, in town squares and depressed neighborhoods. Like a major department store in a mall, libraries attract large numbers of people, creating economic opportunities for numerous businesses and organizations in the surrounding area. Large cities, medium-sized ones, and even small towns have successfully transformed their libraries into the hubs (枢纽) of vibrant neighborhoods.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 以场所为基础的经济发展强调在城镇广场和萧条社区提供有吸引力的、功能性的和以社区为基础的场所的重要性，例如图书馆。就像商场里的大型百货商店一样，图书馆吸引了大量的人流，为周边地区的众多企业和组织创造了经济机会。大城市、中型城市甚至小城镇都成功地将图书馆转变为充满活力的社区的枢纽。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) As key municipal agencies, and focal points for community education, libraries are major players in creating livable, environmentally friendly cities and towns. The Urban Libraries Council released a report detailing the unique ways in which libraries can further sustainability at the local level. Beyond ensuring that library construction projects consider environmental impact, libraries can take a lead in supporting local foods and craftsmen, like the Peabody Institute Library’s partnering with local businesses to pioneer a farmers’ market in their courtyard, or the Richmond Public Library’s seed lending library which “nurtures locally-adapted plant varieties, and fosters community resilience (韧性), self-reliance and a culture of sharing.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 作为主要的市政机构和社区教育的焦点，图书馆是创建宜居、环保的城镇的主要参与者。城市图书馆理事会发布了一份报告，详细介绍了图书馆在地方层面促进可持续发展的独特方式。除了确保图书馆建设项目考虑到环境影响之外，图书馆还可以带头支持当地食品和工匠，例如皮博迪研究所图书馆与当地企业合作，在其庭院中开辟农贸市场，或者里士满公共图书馆的种子借阅图书馆“培育适合当地的植物品种，并培养社区的韧性、自力更生和分享文化”。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Archives preserve historic artifacts, oral histories, digital history projects, and scholarly writings relevant to the community, including minority groups. Communities lucky enough to have archivists have a great advantage when it comes to organizing historical records and artifacts. An organized archive is a place where people can research their ancestry and immigration history, do environmental research, and more. An archivist is an advocate for preservation who, among other things, coordinates the restoration of maps and paintings, the digitization of vital records, and the creation of oral history projects. With projects like the Massachusetts Memories Road Show and the Veterans History Project, evidence of the importance of archives is everywhere.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 档案馆保存与社区（包括少数群体）相关的历史文物、口述历史、数字历史项目和学术著作。幸运地拥有档案管理员的社区在组织历史记录和文物方面具有很大的优势。有组织的档案馆是人们可以研究他们的祖先和移民历史、进行环境研究等的地方。档案管理员是保存的倡导者，除其他外，他负责协调地图和绘画的修复、重要记录的数字化以及口述历史项目的创建。通过马萨诸塞州回忆路演和退伍军人历史项目等项目，档案重要性的证据随处可见。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) In the words of Robert Putnam, “People may go to the library looking mainly for information, but they find each other there.” New moms connect at baby story-times; elderly people, often facing difficult life transitions, attend events and find that they make new friends; teenagers meet up in libraries’ teen spaces after school; and readers discuss current events in the periodicals room. In libraries, community-building connections are happening all the time.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 用罗伯特·普特南的话来说，“人们去图书馆可能主要是为了寻找信息，但他们在那里找到了彼此。”新妈妈们在给宝宝讲故事的时候互相交流；经常面临人生艰难转变的老年人参加活动并发现他们结识了新朋友；青少年放学后在图书馆的青少年空间聚会；读者们在期刊室讨论时事。在图书馆中，社区建设联系一直在发生。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) As Keith Richards said, “The public library is the great equalizer.” Despite the rising costs of concert and theater tickets, public library events (including concerts, author visits, and gallery displays) are often offered free of charge, enabling people of any income level to attend. In addition, library book groups allow people to explore and discuss the literary arts, and the Great Stories Club introduces at-risk youth to literature. The best part: it’s all free and open to the public.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 正如基思·理查兹所说，“公共图书馆是伟大的均衡器。”尽管音乐会和剧院门票的费用不断上涨，但公共图书馆活动（包括音乐会、作者参观和画廊展览）通常是免费的，任何收入水平的人都可以参加。此外，图书馆图书小组让人们探索和讨论文学艺术，而伟大的故事俱乐部则向处于危险中的年轻人介绍文学。最好的部分是：一切都是免费并向公众开放。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) In a time when education is increasingly expensive, public libraries provide information and educational opportunities free for all people, regardless of their socio-economic status. Offered by libraries across the country, American Library Association’s Let’s Talk about It programs are wonderful examples of scholar-facilitated learning opportunities in libraries. In addition, many libraries present classes and discussion programs, and some even provide online continuing education courses such as the Universal Class database.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 在教育费用日益昂贵的时代，公共图书馆为所有人免费提供信息和教育机会，无论其社会经济地位如何。美国图书馆协会的“让我们谈谈它”计划由全国各地的图书馆提供，是图书馆中由学者推动的学习机会的绝佳例子。此外，许多图书馆还提供课程和讨论项目，有的甚至还提供Universal Class数据库等在线继续教育课程。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Librarians know that patrons aren’t just information consumers, they’re information producers. Patrons use the library to gain knowledge in order to create their own new and independent works. Increasing numbers of libraries provide spaces and services that meet the needs of people who want to learn how to edit Wikipedia, set up blogs or podcasts, create their own magazines, and so much more. Many libraries offer art or writing workshops and groups, and some provide music practice rooms for patrons. Programs like ImaginOn in Charlotte, North Carolina, provide exciting models that take community partnership, creativity, and creation to a new level.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 图书馆员知道顾客不仅仅是信息消费者，他们还是信息生产者。读者利用图书馆获取知识，以便创作自己的新的独立作品。越来越多的图书馆提供空间和服务，满足那些想要学习如何编辑维基百科、建立博客或播客、创建自己的杂志等等的人们的需求。许多图书馆提供艺术或写作研讨会和团体，有些还为顾客提供音乐练习室。像北卡罗来纳州夏洛特市的 ImaginOn 这样的项目提供了令人兴奋的模式，将社区合作、创造力和创造提升到一个新的水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) The decline of civil discourse stems in part from the fact that it is so easy for people to watch news about, buy products from, and engage — in both the virtual and real worlds — only with those of similar backgrounds and ideologies. Public libraries, through such programs as The Human Library and Socrates Café, can help build small communities of difference that encourage people to interact with and learn from each other through dialogue. By both actively promoting civil discourse through these programs, and modeling and upholding the principles of free inquiry and expression for all, libraries help individuals rediscover the importance of and increased need for civil discourse in American life.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 公民话语的衰落部分源于这样一个事实：人们很容易在虚拟世界和现实世界中观看新闻、购买产品并参与其中，但前提是具有相似背景和意识形态的人。公共图书馆通过人类图书馆和苏格拉底咖啡馆等项目，可以帮助建立差异化的小社区，鼓励人们通过对话进行互动和相互学习。通过这些项目积极促进公民话语，并树立和维护所有人自由探究和表达的原则，图书馆帮助个人重新发现公民话语在美国生活中的重要性和日益增长的需求。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Free tutoring, homework help programs, and summer reading programs for kids and teens help bridge the economic divide that impacts students’ academic performance. The cost of hiring a private tutor is well beyond what many library patrons can afford, so libraries offer homework help and tutoring online, by phone, in person, and even through social media and homework apps. Annual summer reading programs also have a positive impact on student performance and, according to a 2010 study conducted by Dominican University’s Graduate School of Library and Information Science, students’ reading skills get a boost from these popular nationwide events.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 为儿童和青少年提供的免费辅导、家庭作业帮助计划和暑期阅读计划有助于弥合影响学生学业成绩的经济鸿沟。聘请私人导师的费用远远超出了许多图书馆顾客的承受能力，因此图书馆通过在线、电话、面对面，甚至通过社交媒体和家庭作业应用程序提供家庭作业帮助和辅导。一年一度的夏季阅读计划也对学生的表现产生积极影响，根据多米尼加大学图书馆与信息科学研究生院 2010 年进行的一项研究，学生的阅读技能从这些受欢迎的全国性活动中得到了提高。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Through library collections, programs, and physical spaces, children learn to share, to be engaged in their communities, to participate in the arts, and to explore their immediate world and the world at large. There are surely endless examples of innovative library services for children, including the Middle Country Public Library’s Nature Explorium, which engages children in learning about the natural world.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 通过图书馆藏书、项目和物理空间，孩子们学会分享、参与社区、参与艺术、探索眼前的世界和整个世界。为儿童提供创新图书馆服务的例子肯定不胜枚举，其中包括中部国家公共图书馆的自然探索馆，它让孩子们了解自然世界。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) These examples are just a few of the many amazing things that public libraries around the United States (and the world) are doing to build and maintain strong community connections. We encourage you to try some of these ideas in your own libraries, and we hope that these ideas will help you be better able to convince your community leaders of the important role that public libraries play in communities large and small.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 这些例子只是美国（和世界各地）公共图书馆为建立和维持强大的社区联系所做的许多令人惊奇的事情中的一小部分。我们鼓励您在自己的图书馆中尝试其中一些想法，我们希望这些想法将帮助您更好地说服社区领导公共图书馆在大大小小的社区中发挥的重要作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. People going to the library in search of information can build connections with each other there.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 去图书馆查找信息的人们可以在那里建立彼此的联系。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. According to advocates of libraries as community builders, librarians are not doing their job well if they do not change their communities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 图书馆作为社区建设者的倡导者认为，如果图书馆员不改变社区，他们就没有做好自己的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. With the costs of education continually rising, public libraries remain places where all people can have access to education.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 随着教育费用不断上涨，公共图书馆仍然是所有人都能接受教育的场所。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Libraries draw large crowds, thus creating lots of business opportunities in neighboring areas.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 图书馆吸引了大量人群，从而为邻近地区创造了大量商机。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. With the world more and more digitalized, people sometimes underestimate the role of libraries as community and cultural centers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 随着世界越来越数字化，人们有时会低估图书馆作为社区和文化中心的作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Various programs organized by public libraries for children and adolescents help narrow the gap between students from varying economic backgrounds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 公共图书馆为儿童和青少年举办的各种方案有助于缩小不同经济背景的学生之间的差距。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. In an organized archive, people can do research on their family history and find out how their ancestors came to settle in the new land.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 在有组织的档案中，人们可以研究他们的家族历史，并了解他们的祖先如何来到新的土地上定居。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Public libraries organize cultural events, often allowing people of different income levels to attend free of charge.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 公共图书馆组织文化活动，通常允许不同收入水平的人免费参加。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Besides being an information provider, the library performs many other important services for the community.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 除了提供信息外，图书馆还为社区提供许多其他重要服务。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Public libraries can help build small communities of people with different backgrounds and ideologies.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 公共图书馆可以帮助建立由不同背景和意识形态的人们组成的小社区。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Nationally, one in six children miss 15 or more days of school in a year. Education officials have deplored all this missed instruction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在全国范围内，六分之一的儿童每年缺课 15 天或以上。教育官员对所有这些错过的指导表示遗憾。

paragraphs.sourceText: These chronically absent students suffer academically because of all the classroom instruction they miss out on. In 2015, the US secretary of education responded to this crisis, urging communities to support every student to attend every day and be successful in school. His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason — excused or unexcused — is a primary cause of low academic achievement.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些长期缺席的学生由于错过了所有课堂教学而在学业上受到影响。 2015年，美国教育部长对这一危机做出了回应，敦促社区支持每个学生每天上课并在学校取得成功。他的公开信指出，一年中因任何原因缺课 10%（有故或无故）是学业成绩低下的主要原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: Worrying about whether children attend school makes sense. After all, if students don’t show up, teachers can’t teach them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 担心孩子是否上学是有道理的。毕竟，如果学生不出现，老师就无法教他们。

paragraphs.sourceText: But what if America’s attendance crisis is about much more than students missing class? What if, instead, it is a reflection of family and community crises these students face — such as being ejected from the family apartment, fearing for their safety in their neighborhood or suffering an illness?
paragraphs.translationZh: 但如果美国的出勤危机不仅仅是学生缺课呢？相反，如果这反映了这些学生面临的家庭和社区危机——例如被赶出家庭公寓、担心自己在社区的安全或患病，该怎么办？

paragraphs.sourceText: As social scientists we investigated how excused and unexcused absences relate to children’s academic achievement.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为社会科学家，我们研究了有故和无故缺勤与儿童学业成绩的关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children’s learning. In fact, children with no unexcused absences — but 15 to 18 excused absences — have test scores equal to their peers who have no absences.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们发现，家长借口缺勤对孩子的学习影响不大。事实上，没有无故缺勤的孩子——但有 15 到 18 次无故缺勤的孩子——的考试成绩与没有缺勤的同龄人相同。

paragraphs.sourceText: Meanwhile, the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与此同时，即使只有一次无故缺勤的孩子，其学业成绩也比没有缺勤的同龄人要差得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships. Unexcused absences can be a powerful signal of how those out-of-school challenges affect children’s academic progress.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们认为，无故缺席是儿童和家庭面临的许多挑战的强烈信号，包括经济和医疗困难。无故缺勤可能是一个强有力的信号，表明这些校外挑战如何影响儿童的学业进步。

paragraphs.sourceText: Our evidence suggests unexcused absences are problematic, but for a different reason than people often think. Absence from school, and especially unexcused absence, matters mainly as a signal of many crises children and their families may be facing. It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们的证据表明，无故缺勤是有问题的，但其原因与人们通常认为的不同。缺课，尤其是无故缺课，主要是儿童及其家庭可能面临许多危机的信号。由于缺课而导致学生成绩下降，这并不重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: How we choose to think of school absences matters for educational policy. School attendance policies typically hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss, regardless of whether they were excused or unexcused absences.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们如何选择考虑学校缺勤对教育政策至关重要。学校出勤政策通常要求学校和家庭对孩子缺课的日子负责，无论缺课是有理由的还是无故的。

paragraphs.sourceText: These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically because they are missing classroom instruction. They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences. We find neither to be the case.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些政策假定，因任何原因缺课都会损害儿童的学业，因为他们缺席了课堂教学。他们还认为学校将能够通过减少学生缺勤来进行有效干预。我们发现情况并非如此。

paragraphs.sourceText: As a result, these attendance policies end up disproportionately punishing families dealing with out-of-school crises in their lives and pressuring schools who serve them to get students to school more often.
paragraphs.translationZh: 结果，这些出勤政策最终对那些面临失学危机的家庭造成了不成比例的惩罚，并迫使为他们服务的学校让学生更频繁地上学。

paragraphs.sourceText: We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.
paragraphs.translationZh: 相反，我们建议使用无故缺勤作为信号，将资源分配给最需要资源的儿童和家庭。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: After earning a bachelor’s degree, I was determined to do what I love. I headed straight to graduate school to investigate the social problems that fascinated me.
paragraphs.translationZh: 获得学士学位后，我决心做自己喜欢的事情。我直接进入研究生院，研究令我着迷的社会问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. “Follow your passion,” I counseled. “You can figure out the employment stuff later.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 近十年来，我告诉我遇到的每个人他们也应该这样做。 “追随你的热情，”我建议道。 “就业的事情你可以稍后再想。”

paragraphs.sourceText: It wasn’t until I began to research this widely accepted career advice that I understood how problematic it really was.
paragraphs.translationZh: 直到我开始研究这个被广泛接受的职业建议，我才明白它到底有多大问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: As a sociologist, I interviewed college students and professional workers to learn what it really meant to pursue their dreams, which I will refer to here as the passion principle. I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为一名社会学家，我采访了大学生和专业工作者，以了解追求梦想的真正含义，我在这里将其称为激情原则。在我的新书研究中发现的这一原理让我感到震惊。

paragraphs.sourceText: Surveys show the American public has long held the passion principle in high regard as a career decision-making priority. And its popularity is even stronger among those facing job instability.
paragraphs.translationZh: 调查显示，美国公众长期以来一直高度重视激情原则，并将其作为职业决策的优先事项。在那些面临工作不稳定的人中，它的受欢迎程度甚至更高。

paragraphs.sourceText: Advocates of the passion principle found it compelling because they believed that following one’s passion can provide workers with both the motivation necessary to work hard and a place to find fulfillment.
paragraphs.translationZh: 激情原则的倡导者发现它很有吸引力，因为他们相信追随激情可以为员工提供努力工作所需的动力和找到成就感的地方。

paragraphs.sourceText: Yet, what I found is that following one’s passion does not necessarily lead to fulfillment, but is one of the most powerful cultural forces perpetuating overwork. I also found that promoting the pursuit of one’s passion helps perpetuate social inequalities due to the fact that not everyone has the same economic resources to allow them to pursue their passion with ease.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，我发现追随自己的热情并不一定会带来成就感，但却是导致过度劳累的最强大的文化力量之一。我还发现，促进个人对激情的追求有助于延续社会不平等，因为并不是每个人都有相同的经济资源来让他们轻松地追求自己的激情。

paragraphs.sourceText: While the passion principle is broadly popular, not everyone has the necessary resources to turn their passion into a stable, good-paying job. Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime. They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. And they often have access to parents’ social networks to help them find jobs. Surveys revealed that working-class and first-generation college graduates, regardless of their career field, are more likely than their wealthier peers to end up in low-paying unskilled jobs when they pursue their passion.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然激情原则广为流行，但并不是每个人都有必要的资源将他们的激情转化为稳定、高薪的工作。来自富裕家庭的追求激情的人能够更好地等待他们热爱的工作出现，而不必担心学生贷款。他们也更有能力接受无薪实习，以便在父母支付房租的同时踏入职场。他们经常可以访问父母的社交网络来帮助他们找到工作。调查显示，工人阶级和第一代大学毕业生，无论其职业领域如何，在追求自己的激情时，都比富裕的同龄人更有可能从事低薪非技术性工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the “follow your passion” path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大学、工作场所和职业顾问为每个人提倡“追随你的激情”道路，却没有提供公平的竞争环境，这导致了职业抱负者之间长期存在的社会经济不平等。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s not just well-off passion-seekers who benefit from the passion principle. Employers of passionate workers do, too. Potential employers showed greater interest in passionate applicants in part because they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay. They even sacrifice a good salary, job stability and leisure time to work in a job they love.
paragraphs.translationZh: 受益于激情原则的不仅仅是富裕的激情追求者。拥有热情员工的雇主也是如此。潜在雇主对充满热情的求职者表现出更大的兴趣，部分原因是他们相信求职者会在工作中努力工作，而不期望加薪。他们甚至牺牲优厚的薪水、工作的稳定性和闲暇时间来从事自己喜欢的工作。
